while_loop_vs_unroll_outcome.detail: The while-loop form (`while stride > 0u32 { if lid < stride { ... } workgroup_barrier(); stride = lshr(stride, 1u32); }`) compiled cleanly with ZERO HIR errors/warnings on the first attempt: OQ2 (divergent-barrier hard error) did not fire because `conditional_depth` is bumped only by if/else, not while, confirmed by reading axc-hir/src/typecheck.rs's TypeChecker::conditional_depth field doc and the OQ2 firing site (both pre-existing, unmodified code); OQ1 (missing-barrier SET analysis) did not fire either. Verified empirically via a throwaway compile_module_all + spirv-val run before committing to the design, and again in the final AT-2958/2959/2960 tests. The FALLBACK (single-candidate fully-unrolled straight-line tree reduction) was NOT needed.
while_loop_vs_unroll_outcome.unplanned_deviation_discovered: The milestone spec's illustrative shared-hole example puts `?WG` inside `shared[i32, ?WG]`. Empirically, axc-parser's `parse_shared_len` only accepts an unsuffixed integer LITERAL there (no HoleRef support) -- confirmed by directly parsing the pre-existing matmul_shared_f32.axc example, which already relies on this gap and only ever compiles via text substitution, never a raw parse. Since M3.21's new union_module_holes-based discovery (axc optimize/verify/MCP) parses the RAW file first, a hole inside shared[T,N] would break discovery for two_pass_reduce.axc. Fixing the grammar is out of scope (axc-parser is not in the milestone's touched-crates list). Resolution: `?WG` is used ONLY in `@workgroup(?WG,1,1)` (both kernels, single-candidate `?[64]`, matching the spec's own explicitly-authorized single-candidate fallback for a DIFFERENT reason -- OQ1/OQ2, which turned out not to need it); the shared-array size and tree-reduction stride are fixed literals (64/32) matching the sole candidate. AT-2956 is additionally proven via an inline two-kernel string fixture (unit-test level, not the real file) that exercises the literal `shared[i32,?WG]` substitution text the spec describes, directly against `substitute_strategy_holes` -- so the substitution correctness claim is fully covered even though the real example can't exercise it end-to-end.

pcr1_fix.root_cause: substitute_strategy_holes_boundary_safe (crates/axc-driver/src/lib.rs, F1 scan) compared each hole-name candidate via a direct slice `&source[after_q..end]`. The `end <= bytes.len()` bound was checked but `end`'s char-boundary-ness was not: when a candidate name's byte length reached PAST the start of a following multibyte UTF-8 character, `end` landed mid-character and the raw &str slice panicked ('byte index N is not a char boundary') -- a regression from the OLD str::replace algorithm, which silently left such input untouched.
pcr1_fix.exact_code_form_chosen: Replaced `if end <= bytes.len() && &source[after_q..end] == name` with `if source.get(after_q..end) == Some(name)` -- the Option-returning slice form. `str::get` returns `None` for BOTH out-of-bounds and non-char-boundary ranges, so the comparison itself can never panic; a non-char-boundary end can never equal an ASCII hole name anyway, so refusing to match there and falling through to the existing verbatim per-char copy is trivially correct (not merely panic-free, but semantically unchanged for all valid-boundary cases). Chose the `.get()` form over an explicit `source.is_char_boundary(end)` guard because it is shorter, still panic-free by construction (no risk of a future edit dropping the guard), and the review's own fix suggestion listed both as equivalent.
pcr1_fix.other_slices_audit: Audited every `&source[..]` / `source[..]` slice reachable from substitute_strategy_holes_boundary_safe per the review's request. (1) lib.rs ~574: `source[i..]`/`source[i..i+ch_len]` in the verbatim-copy fallback -- `i` is always on a char boundary by induction (starts at 0; each loop iteration either advances by `ch_len = source[i..].chars().next().len_utf8()`, which by definition lands on the next char boundary, or advances to `end` from a match, which is now proven on a char boundary because `source.get(after_q..end)` only returns `Some` for a valid, boundary-aligned range) -- PROVEN SAFE, no change needed. (2) `bytes.get(end)` in the following-byte boundary check reads a single raw byte from the `&[u8]` view, which never panics regardless of UTF-8 structure (byte indexing has no boundary concept) -- SAFE by construction, unaffected by PCR-1. (3) The sibling function strip_strategy_annotation_block (lib.rs ~635/671/672: `&source[at_pos + "@strategy".len()..]`, `&source[..at_pos]`, `&source[close_pos + 1..]`) was also checked even though the review scoped the finding to the F1 scan: `at_pos` comes from a lexer token span (already char-boundary-aligned by construction) with a `starts_with("@strategy")` verification; `"@strategy".len()` is 9 ASCII bytes added past a byte offset already verified to start that exact ASCII string, so the sum lands on a char boundary; `close_pos`/`close_pos+1` come from a byte-scan that only tracks ASCII `{`/`}`, so `+1` is always a boundary too -- PROVEN SAFE, pre-existing and unaffected, no change needed. No other panic-risk slice found in the substitution/strip code path.
pcr1_fix.at_2968c: Two new tests added directly after AT-2968b in crates/axc-driver/src/lib.rs's test module: (1) at_2968c_multibyte_boundary_no_panic_comment_untouched -- reproduces the review's exact fixture (a `//` comment containing `?W` immediately followed by `€`, WG registered as a hole name whose length reaches 1 byte into `€`'s 3-byte encoding); asserts the low-level scan does not panic and leaves the truncated candidate verbatim, AND that the whole module still compiles clean end-to-end via compile_source_with_assignments (SPIR-V magic + workgroup_size correct). (2) at_2968c_multibyte_adjacent_hole_substitutes_correctly -- a REAL multibyte-adjacent hole (`?WG€`, full-length match landing exactly on the char boundary before `€`) still substitutes to `128€`, proving the fix does not overcorrect into refusing valid matches.
